operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case identifiers: City_ID, Match_ID, Host_City, Hanyu_Pinyin, Regional_Population — must be double-quoted with original case.
DDL uses backtick-quoted FK refs (`City_ID`) inside CREATE TABLE; sqlite_master text must be replayed verbatim.
hosting_city.Host_City is declared TEXT but stores integer city ids ('1','2','6','12','11') — storage class contradicts declared type; FK to city.City_ID (INT).
hosting_city.Year is PK but semantically a year (2008..2013); declared INT dispatches to Number fuzzer, not Year fuzzer (type is 'INT' not 'YEAR').
match.Date is TEXT storing '18 February 1992' / '4 April 1993' — text-stored dates, day-month-name-year format, not ISO; String fuzzer will not produce these.
match.Score/Result mix ASCII hyphen '1-0' and en-dash '1–0' — two distinct spellings of the same score.
temperature has no 'May' column (Jan..Apr, Jun..Dec) — month set is incomplete; queries may reference May and fail.
temperature.City_ID FK to city.City_ID; only 8 of 13 cities have temperature rows (partial coverage, not all parents used).
hosting_city has two FKs (Match_ID->match, Host_City->city) plus PK Year; table order must place city and match before hosting_city.
All tables tiny (city 13, match 6, temperature 8, hosting_city 6) — choose_table_sizes will inflate to 30..2500 rows, far above original.
No NOT NULL constraints anywhere (notnull=0 on every column) — TS will freely emit NULLs; original has null_rate 0.0 everywhere.
City text values contain parenthesized region 'Nanjing ( Jiangsu )' and Hanzi contains '/' variants '苏州/ 蘇州' — multi-form strings.
operator_ts_expectations: City_ID/Match_ID/Year/Regional_Population/GDP/temperature months -> Number fuzzer: uniform in [-10^scale,10^scale] (INT scale 0 => [-1,1] mostly, REAL scale 4 => [-10000,10000]) then +-1/+-2 perturbation; implausible for ids, populations, GDP, temperatures.
City/Hanzi/Hanyu_Pinyin/Venue/Competition/Score/Result -> String fuzzer: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length 0..20 plus contamination; will not resemble Chinese text, pinyin, or '1-0' scores.
match.Date declared TEXT -> String fuzzer (not Date fuzzer), so no '18 February 1992'-style values; date predicates on this column get random strings -> FN.
hosting_city.Host_City declared TEXT -> String fuzzer, but FK to city.City_ID (INT) means fill_foreign_keys_consistently draws integer city ids into a TEXT column — matches original storage, good.

FK child columns (temperature.City_ID, hosting_city.Match_ID, hosting_city.Host_City) draw from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement -> duplicates and NULLs when parent empty; ties/duplicates likely where original had none (FP on DISTINCT/COUNT).
PK filtering (sample_fresh_primary_keys) keeps first occurrence; Year PK gets fresh Number draws in [-1,1] mostly -> many duplicate Years dropped, tiny hosting_city.
Number list-range quirk (list_max overwritten to full max) means literal-pool values like 2008, 23019148 do not constrain the upper end -> implausible large ids.
String contamination (+5 chars, drop first/last) will corrupt '1-0' scores and city names -> joins on City text likely miss (FN).
p=0.2 default with 0.3 chance of p=0 per instance: some instances are pure-element (near-original) and some pure-fresh (garbage) — high variance across the 800 units.
max_l0 cap (rng*30) reuses fresh draws after ~30 distinct values -> repeated implausible numbers, may create accidental ties (FP on GROUP BY).
Empty parent (e.g. if city filtered to 0 rows) yields NULL FKs -> temperature/hosting_city rows with NULL City_ID, breaking joins (FN).
temperature month columns are independent Number samplers — no monotonic seasonal structure; range predicates like 'Jan > Feb' get random truth values (FP/FN).
